newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf CEO says deal to boost earnings.
newsitem.headline: Gulf CEO says deal to boost earnings.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd Chief Executive J.P. Bryan said on Monday that his firm's friendly deal to acquire Stampeder Exploration Ltd would have a neutral effect on its cash flow per share but increase earnings per share.
"It will definitely be accretive to earnings," Bryan said in a telephone interview. He did not say by how much.

He also said he doubted the chances of a rival bidder for Stampeder surfacing because of the offer's structure, which includes a C$20 million break-up fee to Gulf if it is not successful in acquiring Stampeder.

"If anybody else bids for it, I'd say they're just stupid, I mean somebody that doesn't have any presense in Canada," Bryan said. "If it's somebody that's already here that can see some real synergy, there could be a reason. But they're going to have to pay a dear price for it."
Gulf said today it agreed to acquire Stampeder in a friendly stock swap deal valued at about C$1 billion. The price includes about C$300 milion of Stampeder debt.
Gulf, which last month was outbid by PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd for CS Resources Ltd, said it would offer 0.69124 of a Gulf share for each Stampeder share.
The offer represented a 31 percent premium over Stampeder's closing stock price of C$5.70 on Friday, Gulf said.

Bryan said his vision for Stampeder was similar to that for CS, which included folding in Gulf's heavy oil and oil sands assets with the target firm's heavy oil operations for a possible public offering of a stand-alone entity.
But Stampeder offered the benefit of other operations in light oil and natural gas, which made up about 55 percent of the company, he said.
He said he believed the offer was about equal to Stampeder's net asset value.
"We certainly think we're paying a full price but we don't think we've reached beyond our ability to add value here," Bryan said.
The offer proved that Gulf could strike a friendly takeover deal after a spate of hostile ones, Bryan said.
